item.title: Nadi Women thrash Rewa 100–0 in Marama Cup clash
item.description: The Nadi women’s rugby team thrashed Rewa 100-0 in their Round 11 Subrails Marama Cup match at Prince Charles Park today. Nadi dominated Rewa in all phases of the game, as the scorching heat took its toll on the Rewa players.
item.content:encoded:
The Nadi women’s rugby team thrashed Rewa 100-0 in their Round 11 Subrails Marama Cup match at Prince Charles Park today.

Nadi dominated Rewa in all phases of the game, as the scorching heat took its toll on the Rewa players.

With the home crowd firmly behind them, Nadi took a commanding 60–0 lead into half-time.

They extended their advantage by scoring another 40 points in the second half to seal a comprehensive victory.

Meanwhile, Tailevu is currently playing Macuata at Subrail Park in Labasa.

item.title: Wearing the Fiji Bati jersey brings a special sense of pride for Navale
item.description: Fiji Bati player Caleb Navale says wearing the national jersey brings him a special sense of pride as it represents his culture, family and everyone who has supported him throughout his journey. The Manly Sea Eagles player says it is difficult to put into words what wearing the Fiji Bati jersey means to him, as the feeling is different from wearing any other jersey.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Bati player Caleb Navale says wearing the national jersey brings him a special sense of pride as it represents his culture, family and everyone who has supported him throughout his journey.

The Manly Sea Eagles player says it is difficult to put into words what wearing the Fiji Bati jersey means to him, as the feeling is different from wearing any other jersey.

Navale says the support from his family, fans and the Fijian community makes representing the country even more special.

With the Rugby League World Cup approaching, Navale says it feels surreal to finally be preparing for a tournament he has been thinking about for the past four years.

He says the players are excited and ready to begin their World Cup campaign.

Navale says preparations have been going well since the team arrived in Fiji on Monday.

He says several players are visiting Fiji for the first time and have enjoyed exploring the country and meeting people through the team's community activities.

Navale has also thanked supporters for the messages of encouragement the Fiji Bati have already received.

He says the players hear the messages of support, which mean a lot to the team as they prepare for the World Cup.

Meanwhile, the Rugby League World Cup gets underway next Thursday, with Australia facing New Zealand in the opening match at 9.05pm.

The Fiji Bati will open their campaign against the Cook Islands next Sunday at 5.05pm at McDonald Jones Stadium in Newcastle.

They will then take on Australia on the 25th at 9.05pm before wrapping up their pool matches against New Zealand on the 31st at 4.30pm.

item.title: Fusi Feaunati appointed Head of Womens Rugby
item.description: Fusi Feaunati has been appointed as the new Head of Women's Rugby in Fiji and he starts in his role today. FRU High Performance Manager, Nacanieli Cawanibuka, says the appointment marks an important step in the Unions commitment to investing in the growth and development of women's rugby.
item.content:encoded:
Fusi Feaunati has been appointed as the new Head of Women's Rugby in Fiji and he starts in his role today.

FRU High Performance Manager, Nacanieli Cawanibuka, says the appointment marks an important step in the Unions commitment to investing in the growth and development of women's rugby.

Cawanibuka says the appointment reflects FRU's commitment to moving the women's game into its next phase of development.

He says the new coach brings experience across different levels of the women's game, and his role will help piece together and establish a higher performance environment that is distinctly different and professionally driven.

Cawanibuka says their ambition for women's rugby is to become a valuable part of the FRFU competitively, socially and commercially.

He says Fusi's experience includes serving as Women's and Girls Lead with Wellington Rugby Football Union, Leadership and Coaching roles with Wellington Pride, Head Coach and Assistant Coach roles with Hurricanes Poua, Black Ferns Wellington Hub Manager with New Zealand Rugby and performance and development roles with Manawatu Rugby Union.

item.title: Tailevu finds a taste of home in Taveuni ahead of Skipper Cup clash
item.description: Tailevu may be hundreds of kilometres away from home, but the players have been reminded that support for the team extends beyond provincial boundaries after members of the Tailevu community living in Taveuni visited them in camp. The Tailevu rugby team is currently in camp at Wairiki as they prepare for their Skipper Cup clash against Taveuni tomorrow.
item.content:encoded:
Tailevu may be hundreds of kilometres away from home, but the players have been reminded that support for the team extends beyond provincial boundaries after members of the Tailevu community living in Taveuni visited them in camp.

The Tailevu rugby team is currently in camp at Wairiki as they prepare for their Skipper Cup clash against Taveuni tomorrow.

People with connections to Tailevu through their parents, grandparents, marriage or vasu ties visited the players, bringing a little piece of home to the team.

Members of the Nadroga-Navosa community living in Taveuni, along with traditional leaders and women from Taveuni, also joined the gathering.

The team says the visit showed that the bonds of the vanua extend beyond rugby and the jersey, with people continuing to support the players even when they are far from home.

They also thanked the Dra VakaTailevu community residing in Nayavu and Wairiki, as well as Nadroga-Navosa Taveuni, for their support.

The team also acknowledged Merridian Store and the Niumataiwalu family from Dre’eti, Qamea, for their contributions.

Tailevu says the support has helped the players remain grounded and united as they continue preparations for this weekend's match.

Tailevu is currently third on the Skipper Cup points table with 38 points, while Taveuni is seventh with 25 points.

Nadi moved to the top of the table following their 27-23 victory last Saturday.

Tailevu will take on Taveuni at the Wairiki School Grounds this Saturday.
